# get_relevant_context: pure-symbolic context retrieval via entity index (topic) or list-all (no topic)

Commit bddba142 (M1 completion) adds the `get_relevant_context` MCP tool and its supporting graph layer: `relevant_context()`, `list_instances()`, `build_context_item()`, and the public `ContextItem` struct. When a non-empty topic is provided the tool searches via the cache-coherent entity index (`entity_index.search_classes()`); when the topic is omitted or blank it enumerates all instances of the ontology's classes in the project KG graph via SPARQL quad iteration. Explicitly pure-symbolic: no LLM call on the retrieval path (tool description: "Symbolic — no LLM"). Returns structured ContextItem objects (kind, label, literal properties, IRI) formatted as a readable block by `format_context()`. Limit is clamped to 1–100 at the MCP layer. Test: `tests/context.rs` (hermetic, two-decision fixture; both list-all and topic-filtered paths exercised). Completes M1: live tools are `ping`, `record_important_decision`, `query` (+trace), `get_relevant_context`; 5 tests green, clippy clean. Record → restart → read-back across two separate processes (shared data dir) also verified.

# Benchmark content parity: B1 export carries exactly the records B2 reads from the graph

Commit 7633402925 (`bench/export_corpus.py`, `bench/parity_check.py`). The B1 free-text chunks and the B2 graph arm must carry **identical knowledge** — the same records, same descriptions — so the headline B2−B1 comparison isolates retrieval mechanism rather than knowledge content. 

Implementation: `export_corpus.py` pulls every record from the project graph via a deterministic SPARQL SELECT over `kg/project` (predicates matched by local-name via STRENDS, per the decouple-code-from-ontology-ttl lesson). It deliberately does NOT use `get_relevant_context` for this, because that tool is relevance-ranked and hard-capped at 100 items (`src/mcp/mod.rs: clamp(1,100)`) — it is a retrieval surface, not a bulk dump. SPARQL is the correct bulk-read primitive here.

`parity_check.py` enforces the invariant: chunk count == graph record count, every chunk IRI exists in the graph, and each chunk's body text matches the graph's `hasDescription` for that record. A mismatch means B1 and B2 would not carry identical knowledge — confounding the experiment.

# get_relevant_context topic search: search_records (BM25 over label + description) replaces search_classes (label-only)

Commit caa6e387e6 (Merge search-records-integration). src/graph/mod.rs relevant_context(): entity_index.search_classes(t, &class_iris, &state.store, &data_graphs, moose::LABEL_PREDICATES, limit) replaced by entity_index.search_records(t, &class_iris, &state.store, &data_graphs, &text_fields, limit). text_fields = [(moose::RDFS_LABEL, 2.0_f32), (state.capture.description.as_str(), 1.0_f32)] — rdfs:label weighted 2× because every record carries it as its title; description weighted 1×. Searching rdfs:label rather than hasTitle ensures label-only records (no hasTitle) are still found and the title text isn't double-counted. BM25 is raw/corpus-relative — results are ranked and top-k selected rather than filtered by an absolute score. List-all path (no topic → list_instances via SPARQL) is unchanged. Tool remains purely symbolic: no LLM on the retrieval path.

# Relational expansion in get_relevant_context must be bounded: budgeted reach, not neighborhood dump

Commit 5dc4a3ba00 (src/graph/mod.rs, EXPAND_FROM_TOP/EXPAND_MAX_HOPS/EXPAND_MAX constants). Relational expansion in get_relevant_context is a budgeted reach to the few linked records that complete an answer — specifically the lexically-distant neighbor that BM25 alone misses — without dumping the full neighborhood. Concretely: expansion seeds from only the top-N BM25 hits (EXPAND_FROM_TOP=3), walks at most EXPAND_MAX_HOPS=2 hops outward, and appends at most EXPAND_MAX=5 total linked records. Context efficiency is the whole point of get_relevant_context: returning the entire reachable neighborhood would negate the retrieval tool's purpose of surfacing the most relevant records without overwhelming the caller's context window. Expansion is skipped entirely for list-all calls and when MOOSEDEV_EXPAND_HOPS=0.

# Benchmark oracle mode: harness-side retrieval isolates knowledge-value from fetch-willingness

Commit 29cac60c28 (`bench/run.py`). A `mode="oracle"` parameter on `run_cell()` causes the harness to retrieve relevant knowledge and prepend it verbatim to the prompt, without giving the agent a live memory tool. This isolates two confounds: H8 (fetch-willingness — whether the agent chooses to call the memory tool) and knowledge-value (whether the knowledge itself helps). If oracle does not beat B0, the captured knowledge has no value; if live-tool < oracle, the gap is fetch-willingness alone.

Implementation: `oracle_context()` calls `get_relevant_context` for B2 (current-only, symbolic BM25); `freetext_oracle_context()` runs BM25 over the exported chunk file for B1 arms (currency-blind — superseded chunks are retrievable, same as what a B1-rag agent would get). Topic is `task["memory_topic"] or task["prompt"]` — a focused subject phrase so the retrieval signal is unambiguous.

Oracle asymmetry is intentional: the B2−B1 oracle delta isolates B2's currency-awareness (the agent acting on lifecycle status) rather than information withholding (B1 oracle would also retrieve superseded chunks, so if B2 oracle correctly ignores a superseded record and B1 oracle uses it, that gap is earned).

item.text: `get_relevant_context` currently does a pure-symbolic top-k BM25 search over the entity index for the supplied topic, scoring records from text fields like `rdfs:label` and description and returning the best matches as structured context items. That matches the recorded note titled `get_relevant_context topic search: search_records (BM25 over label + description) replaces search_classes (label-only)`, and the no-topic path falls back to listing all instances.
